1. Project and Package Creation Purpose: This step creates a container for the ETL workflow where all data flow components will reside. Step Description: • I opened Visual Studio 2026 Community and created a new Integration Services Project named “SSIS_Transformation_Lab” • Visual Studio automatically created a default SSIS package called Package.dtsx that I later renamed to “CustomerETL.dtsx” where I will design my ETL process. 2. Adding a Data Flow Task Purpose: The Data Flow Task is the main container for moving data from source to destination while applying transformations. Step Description: • In the Control Flow tab, I dragged a Data Flow Task from the SSIS Toolbox into the design area. • I renamed it to “Customer Data” 3. Adding the Source (ADO NET Source) Purpose: This step reads raw customer data from the database and passes it to the next transformation. Step Description: • In the Data Flow tab, I dragged ADO NET Source into the design area. • Configured it to connect to my SQL Server database BikeStores. • Selected the Sales.Customer table as the source. 4. Derived Column Transformation The Derived Column transformation allows you to create new columns or modify existing columns by applying expressions or calculations. It is used to shape and manipulate data as it flows through the ETL process. Purpose: The Derived Column allows creating new calculated columns or modifying existing ones. In this case, it combines first and last names. Step Description: • Dragged Derived Column into the Data Flow area. • Connected the ADO NET Source to the Derived Column using the blue arrow. • Configured a new column “FullName” as (first_name + " " + last_name) 5. Conditional Split Transformation The Conditional Split transformation directs data rows to different outputs based on defined conditions. It is useful for categorizing or filtering data within the data flow according to specific rules. Purpose: Conditional Split filters or routes data based on conditions. Useful for processing subsets differently. Step Description: • Dragged Conditional Split into the Data Flow area. • Connected the Derived Column output to it. • Created a condition state == "NY" to separate NY customers from others. 6. Data Conversion Transformation The Data Conversion transformation is used to change the data type of columns to match the requirements of the destination or other transformations. Step Description: • Dragged Conditional Split into the Data Flow area. • Connected the Derived Column output to it. • Created a condition state == "NY" to separate NY customers from others. 6. Data Conversion Transformation The Data Conversion transformation is used to change the data type of columns to match the requirements of the destination or other transformations. It ensures that the data flows correctly and is compatible with the target schema. Purpose: Data Conversion ensures that data types in the ETL flow match the destination schema. SSIS requires compatible types to avoid errors during insertion. Step Description: • After the Conditional Split, I dragged a Data Conversion transformation into the Data Flow area. • Connected one of the outputs (NY_Customers) from the Conditional Split to the Data Conversion transformation using a blue arrow. • Configured the Data Conversion to change data types and length of “phone” 7. Destination (ADO NET Destination) Step Description: • Dragged ADO NET Destination into the Data Flow area. • Connected the last transformation output to the destination. • Configured it to insert data into “ADO NET Destinationn” table in the database. • Mapped input columns to destination columns. 8. Testing the Package Step Description: • Clicked Start in Visual Studio to execute the package. • Monitored the progress tab to confirm all tasks completed successfully. 9. Sample Output Sample data confirms the Derived Column, Conditional Split, and Data Conversion transformations worked as intended.
